intendedUse: Determine whether introducing coding assistance improved the end-to-end software delivery outcome for one stable service workflow.
workflowBoundary: Work is selected; code is produced; review waits and review work occur; tests and deployment run; failed changes are recovered or reworked; the change reaches production.
workflowCompletion: A change is complete when it reaches production successfully or is abandoned under the same workflow definition used for the baseline.
downstreamHandoffs: Production recovery or rework where required
movedBottleneck: Faster local code generation moved more work into the review queue and increased rework, so code-writing time stopped being the dominant constraint.
unhappyPath: Generated code is produced faster, but reviewers receive larger or more numerous changes, wait time rises, and rework offsets the local task-speed gain.

actors.role: Developers use coding assistance inside the existing review, test, release, and recovery workflow.

authority: Developers may use the assistant to produce code, but existing review and deployment authorities remain unchanged.
accountability: The engineering lead owns the workflow measurement and decides whether to redesign or continue the pilot.
demonstrated: Illustrative median code-production time fell from 120 minutes to 45 minutes, while median review wait rose from 3.5 hours to 7.8 hours, deployment rework rose from 6% to 12%, and median issue-to-production lead time rose from 26 hours to 29 hours.
inferredOrAssumed: A local coding-speed improvement does not imply an end-to-end delivery improvement. The measured end-to-end result in this case moved in the opposite direction.
knownLimitations: The case measures one service workflow and does not establish organisation-wide productivity or economic Value.
Customer outcome and full cost are outside this Outcome decision.
outcomeMeasure: Median issue-to-successful-production lead time for the defined service workflow, with deployment rework rate as a guardrail.
baseline: Eight illustrative pre-pilot weeks for the same service and workflow definition, compared with eight post-introduction weeks using the same measurement definitions.
nextEvidence: Redesign the review and change-size workflow, then repeat the same Outcome measurement before any separate scale or Value decision.
stopRule: Do not report local generation speed as software-delivery productivity. Pause expansion if end-to-end lead time and rework remain worse than baseline.
